cim: FDA clears RadNet AI tool for predicting five-year breast cancer risk from routine mammograms
cim_eredeti: FDA clears RadNet AI tool for predicting five-year breast cancer risk from routine mammograms
szoveg_eredeti:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has cleared a new artificial intelligence product from RadNet Inc., which it says can predict five-year breast cancer risk from a routine mammogram.

Manufactured by subsidiary DeepHealth, leaders believe “Mammo Risk” is the first FDA-cleared, image-based breast cancer risk prediction solution for 3D mammography.

The product is compatible with multiple brands of imaging systems and is able to assess three-, four- and five-year cancer risk, helping to “personalize patient pathways and optimize screening workflows.”

“Unlocking these predictive insights directly from a routine scan means we can reduce uncertainty, giving providers and patients insights into risk years before cancer would be diagnosed and enabling them to personalize care in a way that can truly save lives,” Niccolò Stefani, MD, DeepHealth’s business and product leader of clinical AI, said in a statement Nov. 24.

RadNet said Mammo Risk uses AI trained on 220,000 studies to derive personalized risk insights directly from mammograms. It was tested via an independent, multicenter study involving over 65,000 screening exams across 10 U.S. clinical sites. Mammo Risk demonstrated “strong” predictive performance of future breast cancer risk, the company notes.

The offering joins another five-year breast cancer risk-prediction tool from vendor Clairity, OK’d by the FDA in May 2025. RadNet noted that its product is different, in that it is cleared for use in 3D mammography, which represents most screening mammograms in the U.S. The American Medical Association also has established a Category 3 CPT code, effective Jan. 1, to enable tracking of the utilization of image-based breast cancer risk assessment technologies, RadNet notes.

DataFirst’s Silverback Workflow Engine combines advanced DICOM routing, an integrated HL7 engine, and intelligent workflow orchestration. Newly added Silverback HarmoniX standardizes inconsistent DICOM study and series descriptions to improve hanging protocol consistency, image presentation, and downstream radiology workflows—all within one unified enterprise imaging platform featured at RSNA 2026.

When he happened upon the CIVIE booth at RBMA PaRADigm 2025, Mina Mousa, MD, had no thoughts of leaving his job at 10-physician Radiology Associates of Tallahassee in Florida.

A small step for technologists. A meaningful step toward patient-centered contrast dosing. And a benefit that can extend to radiologists.
